Since they worship their Lord, devote themselves to His service, and do not disobey Him for the blink of an eye, He swore by them concerning His divinity, saying: {Indeed, your God is One}: He has no partner in divinity. So devote to Him love, fear, hope, and all other kinds of worship.

Verse 5: {Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts}; that is, He is the Creator of these creatures, the Provider for them, and the Manager of them. Just as He has no partner in His lordship over them, so He has no partner in His divinity. Allah often establishes the oneness of divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah) through the oneness of lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah), because the latter points to the former. The polytheists also acknowledged this in worship, so they are bound by what they acknowledged regarding what they denied. Allah singled out the easts for mention because they indicate the wests, or because they are the risings of the stars that He will mention next. Hence He said:

Verses 6–9: {Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the adornment of the stars. And as protection against every rebellious devil. They cannot listen to the highest assembly}: Allah mentioned two great benefits of the stars. The first: they are an adornment for the sky, for were it not for them, the sky would be a dark body without light; but He adorned it with them so that its expanses would be illuminated, its form made beautiful, people would be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea, and the benefits that do result would be achieved. The second: the guarding of the sky against every rebellious devil who, through his defiance, would reach to listen to the highest assembly, namely the angels. Whenever he listens, he is pelted with piercing meteors {from every side}, as a repulsion and a driving away from hearing what the highest assembly says. {And for them is a perpetual punishment}; that is, a lasting one prepared for them because of their rebellion against the obedience of their Lord.

Verse 10: Had Allah not made an exception, that would have been evidence that they do not hear anything at all. But He said: {except one who snatches a fragment}; that is, except one who snatches from the rebellious devils a single word, stealthily and by theft, {and is pursued by a piercing flame}. Hence He said: {Indeed, We created them from sticky clay}; that is, strong and firm, as in His saying, the Exalted: {And We certainly created man from clay of sounding dry mud, altered black mud}.

{12} "Nay, you marvel" (O Messenger, or O human being) at the denial of those who denied the Resurrection, after you had shown them the great signs and the sound proofs. In truth, this is a matter of wonder and astonishment, for it is something that does not admit of denial. "And" more marvelous than their denial, and more emphatic than it, is that they "mock" the one who brought the news of the Resurrection. Mere denial was not enough for them; they added mockery to the true word.

{13} "And" it is also a marvel that when they are "reminded" of what they already recognize in their natural disposition (fitrah) and their intellects, and are alerted to it and have their attention drawn to it, "they do not heed" it. If this is ignorance, it is among the clearest indications of their great dullness, since they are reminded of what is fixed in natural disposition and known by reason, something that admits no doubt. If it is willful ignorance and obstinacy, then it is even more wondrous and strange.

{14} It is also a marvel that when the proofs are set before them, and they are reminded of the signs before which the most capable men bow and the minds of the intelligent submit, they mock them and wonder at them.

{15} It is also a marvel that they say of the truth when it has come to them: "This is nothing but evident magic." They have placed the highest and most exalted of things, which is the truth, in the rank of the basest and most contemptible of things.

{16–17} It is also a marvel that they liken the power of the Lord of the earth and the heavens to the power of a human being, who is deficient in every respect, saying by way of disbelief and denial: "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again? Or our forefathers of old?"

{18} When this was the furthest reach of what they had and the extent of what they possessed, God commanded His Messenger to answer them with a reply that includes intimidation, so He said: "Say: Yes," you will be resurrected, you and your forefathers of old, "and you will be humbled": abased and debased, unable to resist or defy the power of God.

{19} "It will be but a single shout," when Israfil blows into the Trumpet, and "behold, they will be" raised from their graves, "looking on," just as their creation began. They will be resurrected with all their parts, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised.

{20} In that state they will show regret, shame and loss, and will cry out for destruction and ruin, and "they will say: Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment." Thus they confess what they used to mock in the world.

{21} It will be said to them: "This is the Day of Decision," between the servants concerning the rights between them and their Lord and between them and the rest of creation.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verses 22–26:

{22–23} That is: when they come forth on the Day of Resurrection, witness that which they used to deny, and see that which they used to mock, it will be commanded concerning them: to the Fire by which they used to deny. It will be said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾: themselves, through disbelief, association (shirk) and sins; ﴿and their spouses﴾: those of the same kind as their deeds, each being joined to whoever is like him in action; ﴿and what they used to worship besides Allah﴾: of idols and rivals that they claimed. Gather them all together and ﴿guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾; that is, drive them with harsh driving into Hell.

{24} And after their affair has been determined to be the Fire, and they know that they are among the people of the abode of perdition, it will be said: ﴿Stop them﴾: before you bring them to Hell, ﴿indeed they are to be questioned﴾: about what they used to fabricate in the world, so that their lying and disgrace may become manifest before the witnesses.

{25} It will be said to them: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?﴾: that is, what has befallen you today, and what has come upon you, that none of you helps another or relieves another, after you used to claim in the world that your gods would ward off the punishment from you, relieve you, or intercede for you with Allah?!

{26} So it is as if they do not answer this question, because humiliation and abasement have overcome them, and they have submitted to the punishment of the Fire, humbled themselves, lowered themselves and been struck dumb, so they do not speak. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, today they are the ones who submit.﴾

{37} Hence the Exalted said, refuting their saying: ﴿Rather, he has come with the truth﴾; that is, his coming is true, and what he brought of the law and the Book is true, ﴿and confirmed the messengers﴾; that is, his coming confirmed the messengers. {50-59} When the Exalted mentioned their bliss and the fullness of their joy through food, drink, beautiful spouses and fine gatherings, He mentioned their reminiscing among themselves and their exchanging of talk about past matters, and that they kept on conversing and questioning one another until it led one of them to say: {Indeed, I had a companion}: in the world, who denied the Resurrection and blamed me for believing in it, saying to me: {Are you truly among those who affirm? When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be recompensed?}; i.e., be repaid for our deeds? That is: how can you believe in this remote matter, which is most astonishing, namely that when we are torn apart and become dust and bones, we will be resurrected and returned, then be reckoned and repaid for our deeds? That is: the owner of the garden says to his brothers: this is my story and this is my account, me and my companion. I then reached the bliss you see, which the messengers informed us of, while he has undoubtedly reached the punishment. So {will you look down}: that we may see him, and thereby increase in contentment and joy in what we are in, and that this be by direct sight? The punishment had encompassed him. So he said to him, rebuking him for his state and thanking God for His blessing in saving him from his scheming: {By God, you almost brought me to ruin}; i.e., you would have destroyed me by the doubts you introduced, according to your claim. {And had it not been for the favor of my Lord}: by His making me steadfast upon Islam {I would have been among those brought forth} with you into punishment. {Is it not that we will not die, except our first death, and we will not be punished?} That is said by the believer, rejoicing in God's blessing upon the people of Paradise with eternal abiding and safety from punishment. It is known that the pleasure of the people of knowledge in questioning about knowledge and investigating it is above the pleasures found in the talk of this world; so they have a abundant share of this type, and there occurs for them, through the unveiling of scientific realities in Paradise, what cannot be expressed.

{60} When the Exalted mentioned the bliss of Paradise and described it with these beautiful attributes, He praised it, inspired those who work and urged them to act for it, saying: {Indeed, this is the great triumph}: by which they attained every good and everything souls desire and long for, and by which every harm and hated thing was repelled from them. Is there any triumph sought beyond it? Or is it the ultimate of ultimates and the final end of ends, where the pleasure of the Lord of the earth and the heavens settled upon them, and they rejoiced in His nearness, enjoyed knowing Him, delighted in seeing Him, and were moved by His speech?

{62} "Is that better as hospitality, or the Tree of Zaqqum?" That is: is this bliss which We have described for the people of Paradise better, or the punishment in the Blazing Fire, of all kinds of torment? Which of the two foods is more fitting: the food described in Paradise, or the food of the people of the Fire, which is the "Tree of Zaqqum"?

{63–66} "Indeed, We have made it a trial" — that is, a punishment and a retribution "for the wrongdoers," who wronged themselves through disbelief and disobedience. "Indeed, it is a tree that springs forth from the root of Hellfire" — that is, from its midst. This is its origin and its source: the worst of sources and the most wretched. The worst planting indicates the worst growth and its baseness. For this reason, God has alerted us to its evil through what He mentioned of where it grows and through the description of its fruit, that it is like the heads of devils. So do not ask, after this, about its taste or what it does to their insides and bellies. They have no escape from it and no alternative. Hence He says: "Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it." This is the food of the people of the Fire, and wretched is the food of their food.

{67} Then He mentioned their drink, saying: "Then, indeed, for them upon it" — that is, after this food — "is a mixture of boiling water," meaning water that is extremely hot, having reached the utmost of its heat, as the Exalted said: "If they seek relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place" (18:29), and as the Exalted said: "And they will be given boiling water to drink, which will cut their intestines to pieces" (47:15).

{68} "Then, indeed, their return" — that is, their final destination, their abode and their refuge — "is to the Hellfire," so that they may taste of its severe torment and its great heat, that which there is no greater wretchedness beyond.

{69–73} It is as if it were said: what brought them to this abode? So He said: "Indeed, they found their fathers astray. So they hastened in their footsteps" — that is, they hurried in misguidance. They paid no heed to what the messengers called them to, nor to what the scriptures warned them against, nor to the words of the advisers; rather they opposed them, saying: "Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we are indeed guided by their footsteps." "And certainly most of the earlier peoples went astray before them" — that is, before these addressees — "most of the earlier peoples," and only a few of them believed and were guided. "And We certainly sent among them warners" — who warned them against their error and misguidance. "Then observe how was the end of those who were warned" — their end was destruction, disgrace and humiliation. So let these people beware of persisting in their misguidance, lest there befall them the like of what befell those.

{74} Since those who were warned were not all astray, but among them were those who believed and sincerely devoted their religion to God, God excepted them from destruction, saying: "Except the sincere servants of God" — that is, those whom God chose and singled out with His mercy because of their sincerity, for their end became praiseworthy.

Then He mentioned a model of the ends of the deniers among the nations, saying:

That is: is this bliss which We have described for the people of Paradise better, or the punishment in the Blazing Fire, of all kinds of torment? Which of the two foods is more fitting: the food described in Paradise, or the food of the people of the Fire, which is the "Tree of Zaqqum"?

{63–66} "Indeed, We have made it a trial" — that is, a punishment and a retribution "for the wrongdoers," who wronged themselves through disbelief and disobedience. "Indeed, it is a tree that springs forth from the root of Hellfire" — that is, from its midst. This is its origin and its source: the worst of sources and the most wretched. The worst planting indicates the worst growth and its baseness. For this reason, God has alerted us to its evil through what He mentioned of where it grows and through the description of its fruit, that it is like the heads of devils. So do not ask, after this, about its taste or what it does to their insides and bellies. They have no escape from it and no alternative. Hence He says: "Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it." This is the food of the people of the Fire, and wretched is the food of their food.

{67} Then He mentioned their drink, saying: "Then, indeed, for them upon it" — that is, after this food — "is a mixture of boiling water," meaning water that is extremely hot, having reached the utmost of its heat, as the Exalted said: "If they seek relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place" (18:29), and as the Exalted said: "And they will be given boiling water to drink, which will cut their intestines to pieces" (47:15).

{68} "Then, indeed, their return" — that is, their final destination, their abode and their refuge — "is to the Hellfire," so that they may taste of its severe torment and its great heat, that which there is no greater wretchedness beyond.

{69–73} It is as if it were said: what brought them to this abode? So He said: "Indeed, they found their fathers astray. So they hastened in their footsteps" — that is, they hurried in misguidance. They paid no heed to what the messengers called them to, nor to what the scriptures warned them against, nor to the words of the advisers; rather they opposed them, saying: "Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we are indeed guided by their footsteps." "And certainly most of the earlier peoples went astray before them" — that is, before these addressees — "most of the earlier peoples," and only a few of them believed and were guided. "And We certainly sent among them warners" — who warned them against their error and misguidance. "Then observe how was the end of those who were warned" — their end was destruction, disgrace and humiliation. So let these people beware of persisting in their misguidance, lest there befall them the like of what befell those.

{74} Since those who were warned were not all astray, but among them were those who believed and sincerely devoted their religion to God, God excepted them from destruction, saying: "Except the sincere servants of God" — that is, those whom God chose and singled out with His mercy because of their sincerity, for their end became praiseworthy.

Then He mentioned a model of the ends of the deniers among the nations, saying:

{75–82} He (exalted is He) informs us about His servant and messenger Noah (peace be upon him), the first of the messengers, that when he called his people to God for that long period, his call increased them only in flight. He cried out to his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any dwelling of the disbelievers﴾ — the verse — and he said: ﴿My Lord, help me against the corrupt people.﴾ So God answered him, and He praised Himself, saying: ﴿How excellent are the Responders!﴾ — for the supplications of those who supplicate, and for hearing their devotion and humble entreaty. He answered him with an answer that matched what he asked: He saved him and his family from the great distress, drowned all the disbelievers, and preserved his offspring and descendants in succession. All of mankind is from the descendants of Noah (peace be upon him). He also gave him a good and lasting praise until the time of the later generations. That is because he was a good doer in the worship of the Creator and a benefactor to creation, and this is God's custom (exalted is He) regarding the good doers: that He spreads for them praise in proportion to their goodness. His saying ﴿Indeed he was among Our believing servants﴾ indicates that faith is the highest rank of the servants, and that it encompasses all the legal precepts of religion, its foundations and its branches, because God praised with it His elite creation.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verse 83–113:

{83–84} That is: and among the followers of Noah (peace be upon him), and those who followed his path in prophethood, messengership, calling the creation to Allah and answering supplication, was Abraham the Friend (peace be upon him). {When he came to his Lord with a sound heart}: free from shirk, doubts and desires that prevent perceiving the truth and acting upon it. When the heart of a servant is sound, he is safe from every evil and attains every good.

{85–87} Among its soundness is that it is free from deceiving people, envying them, and other bad character traits. For this reason he advised the people for the sake of Allah, beginning with his father and his people, and said: {When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?"} This is a question in the form of denunciation and a binding of them with proof. {Is it a fabrication, gods other than Allah that you desire?} That is: do you worship, besides Allah, falsehoods that are not gods and are not fit for worship?! {So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?}: that He would do to you (what you deserve) when you have worshipped others along with Him?! This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. In the authentic hadith: "Abraham (peace be upon him) told only three lies: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it,' and his saying about his wife, 'She is my sister.'" The purpose is that he stayed behind from them so that his plot against their gods would be completed. Hence {they turned their backs and departed}. When he found the opportunity, {he turned to their gods}, that is: he went to them secretly and stealthily, {and said} mockingly to them: {"Will you not eat? What is wrong with you that you do not speak?"}. That is: how is it fitting that they be worshipped when they are inferior even to animals that eat and speak, while these are inanimate objects that neither eat nor speak?! {Then he attacked them, striking with the right hand}: that is, he began striking them with his strength and vigour until he reduced them to fragments, except a large one among them, so that they might return to it.

{94–96} {So they came hastening toward him}: that is, they hurried and rushed, intending to lay hands on him after they had searched. {They said: "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers!"} {It was said: "We heard a youth who mentions them, called Abraham."} He says: {"By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone."} So they rebuked and blamed him. He said: {"Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it, so ask them, if they can speak."} {So they returned to themselves and said: "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."} {Then they were turned back upon their heads: "You have certainly known that these do not speak."} He said: {"Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you at all nor harms you...?"} to the end of the verse. And his saying here {"Do you worship what you carve?"}: that is, what you carve with your hands and fashion. So how do you worship them when you are the ones who made them, and leave sincere devotion to Allah, who {created you and what you do}?!

{97–98} {They said: "Build for him a structure"}: that is, a high edifice, and kindle fire in it, {and cast him into the blazing fire}, as requital for what he did in breaking their gods. They intended {a plot against him}: to kill him in the most horrible manner. {So We made them the lowest}: Allah turned their plot back upon their own necks, and made the fire cool and safe for Abraham.

{99} When they did this to him, and he had established the proof against them and excused himself before them, {he said: "Indeed, I am going to my Lord"}: that is, I am emigrating to Him, heading to the blessed land, the land of Sham, {He will guide me}: He will show me what is good for me in my religion and my worldly affairs. And in another verse he said: {"And I will withdraw from you and what you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I will not be unblessed in my calling upon my Lord."}

{100} {"My Lord, grant me"}: a child who would be {among the righteous}. This was when he despaired of his people and saw no good in them; he asked Allah to grant him a righteous son through whom Allah would benefit in his life and after his death.

{101} Allah answered him and said: {So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy}. This is Ishmael (peace be upon him) without doubt; for the good tidings of Isaac is mentioned after it, and because Allah, Exalted, said in the good tidings of Isaac: {So We gave him good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob}. This shows that Isaac is not the one who was sacrificed. Allah described Ishmael (peace be upon him) as forbearing, and this includes patience, good character, breadth of chest, and pardoning those who wrong him.

{102} {Then when he reached with him the age of exertion}: that is, he reached the age to strive alongside him, and attained an age in which he is usually most beloved to his parents; his hardship had gone and his benefit had come. Abraham (peace be upon him) said to him: {"Indeed, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you"}: that is, I have seen in sleep and vision that Allah is commanding me to slaughter you, and the dreams of the prophets are revelation. {So see what you think}: for the command of Allah, Exalted, must be carried out. Ishmael said, patient, seeking reward, pleasing to his Lord and dutiful to his father: {"O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient."} That is: go forward with what Allah has ordered you. He informed his father that he had resolved himself to patience, and he tied that to the will of Allah, Exalted, because nothing happens without the will of Allah.

{103} {And when they had both submitted}: that is, Abraham and his son Ishmael. Abraham was resolved to slaughter his son, the fruit of his heart, in compliance with the command of his Lord and out of fear of His punishment; and the son had resolved himself to patience, finding it easy in obedience to his Lord and in the pleasure of his father. {And he put him down upon his forehead}: that is, Abraham laid Ishmael down on his forehead in order to lay him on his side and slaughter him, having turned him over on his face, lest he look at his face at the time of slaughter.

{104–105} {And We called to him}: in that distressing state and astonishing matter: {"O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision"}: that is, you have done what you were commanded, for you resolved yourself to it, did every means, and nothing remained but to pass the knife over his throat. {Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good}: in Our worship, those who prefer Our pleasure over their own desires.

{106} {Indeed, this}: by which We tested Abraham (peace be upon him), {is truly the manifest trial}: that is, the clear one by which the purity of Abraham and the completeness of his love for his Lord and his intimate friendship were shown. When Allah granted Ishmael to Abraham, he loved him intensely, and he was the Friend of the Merciful. Friendship is the highest kind of love, a station that accepts no sharing, and it requires that all parts of the heart be attached to the Beloved. When a portion of his heart became attached to his son Ishmael, Allah, Exalted, willed to purify his affection and test his friendship, so He commanded him to slaughter what competed his love with the love of his Lord. When he gave precedence to the love of Allah over his own desire, resolved to slaughter him, and what was in the heart of competition was removed, the slaughter remained without benefit; hence He said: {Indeed, this is truly the manifest trial}.

{107} {And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice}: that is, a great sacrifice of sheep was substituted for him, which Abraham slaughtered. It was great: in that it was a ransom for Ishmael, in that it is among the noble acts of worship, and in that it became a sacrifice and a sunnah until the Day of Resurrection.

{108–109} {And We left for him among later generations. Peace be upon Abraham}: that is, We kept for him a true praise among later generations, as he had among the earlier ones; so at every time after Abraham (peace be upon him), he is beloved, honoured and praised. {Peace be upon Abraham}: that is, a greeting upon him, like His saying: {"Say: Praise is to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen."}

{110} {Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good}: in the worship of Allah and in dealing with His creation, that We relieve them of hardships and grant them a good end and good praise.

{111} {Indeed, he was among Our believing servants}: in what Allah commanded belief in, those whose faith reached the degree of certainty, as Allah, Exalted, said: {And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain.}

{112} {And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous}: this is the second good tidings of Isaac, behind whom is Jacob. He was given good news of his existence, his survival, the existence of his offspring, and his being a prophet from among the righteous; these are multiple good tidings.

{113} {And We blessed him and Isaac}: that is, We sent down upon them both blessing, which is growth and increase in their knowledge, their deeds and their offspring. Allah spread from their offspring three great nations: the Arab nation from the offspring of Ishmael, the nation of the Children of Israel, and the nation of the Romans from the offspring of Isaac. {And among their offspring are doers of good and those who clearly wrong themselves}: that is, among them are the righteous and the wicked, the just and the unjust, whose wrongdoing is manifest through their disbelief and polytheism. Perhaps this is to remove a misunderstanding: when He said {And We blessed him and Isaac}, that implied blessing in their offspring, and that part of complete blessing is that all their offspring be doers of good; so Allah informed that among them are doers of good and wrongdoers. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verse 83–113:

When the heart of a servant is sound, he is safe from every evil and attains every good.

{85–87} Among its soundness is that it is free from deceiving people, envying them, and other bad character traits. For this reason he advised the people for the sake of Allah, beginning with his father and his people, and said: {When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?"} This is a question in the form of denunciation and a binding of them with proof. {Is it a fabrication, gods other than Allah that you desire?} That is: do you worship, besides Allah, falsehoods that are not gods and are not fit for worship?! {So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?}: that He would do to you (what you deserve) when you have worshipped others along with Him?! This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. When the heart of a servant is sound, he is safe from every evil and attains every good.

{85–87} Among its soundness is that it is free from deceiving people, envying them, and other bad character traits. For this reason he advised the people for the sake of Allah, beginning with his father and his people, and said: {When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?"} This is a question in the form of denunciation and a binding of them with proof. {Is it a fabrication, gods other than Allah that you desire?} That is: do you worship, besides Allah, falsehoods that are not gods and are not fit for worship?! {So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?}: that He would do to you (what you deserve) when you have worshipped others along with Him?! This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. In the authentic hadith: "Abraham (peace be upon him) told only three lies: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it,' and his saying about his wife, 'She is my sister.'" Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verse 83–113:

{83–84} That is: and among the followers of Noah (peace be upon him), and those who followed his path in prophethood, messengership, calling the creation to Allah and answering supplication, was Abraham the Friend (peace be upon him). {When he came to his Lord with a sound heart}: free from shirk, doubts and desires that prevent perceiving the truth and acting upon it. When the heart of a servant is sound, he is safe from every evil and attains every good.

{85–87} Among its soundness is that it is free from deceiving people, envying them, and other bad character traits. For this reason he advised the people for the sake of Allah, beginning with his father and his people, and said: {When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?"} This is a question in the form of denunciation and a binding of them with proof. {Is it a fabrication, gods other than Allah that you desire?} That is: do you worship, besides Allah, falsehoods that are not gods and are not fit for worship?! {So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?}: that He would do to you (what you deserve) when you have worshipped others along with Him?! This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. In the authentic hadith: "Abraham (peace be upon him) told only three lies: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it,' and his saying about his wife, 'She is my sister.'" The purpose is that he stayed behind from them so that his plot against their gods would be completed. Hence {they turned their backs and departed}. When he found the opportunity, {he turned to their gods}, that is: he went to them secretly and stealthily, {and said} mockingly to them: {"Will you not eat? What is wrong with you that you do not speak?"}. That is: how is it fitting that they be worshipped when they are inferior even to animals that eat and speak, while these are inanimate objects that neither eat nor speak?! {Then he attacked them, striking with the right hand}: that is, he began striking them with his strength and vigour until he reduced them to fragments, except a large one among them, so that they might return to it.

{94–96} {So they came hastening toward him}: that is, they hurried and rushed, intending to lay hands on him after they had searched. {They said: "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers!"} {It was said: "We heard a youth who mentions them, called Abraham."} He says: {"By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone."} So they rebuked and blamed him. So how do you worship them when you are the ones who made them, and leave sincere devotion to Allah, who {created you and what you do}?!

This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. In the authentic hadith: "Abraham (peace be upon him) told only three lies: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it,' and his saying about his wife, 'She is my sister.'" When the heart of a servant is sound, he is safe from every evil and attains every good.

{85–87} Among its soundness is that it is free from deceiving people, envying them, and other bad character traits. For this reason he advised the people for the sake of Allah, beginning with his father and his people, and said: {When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?"} This is a question in the form of denunciation and a binding of them with proof. {Is it a fabrication, gods other than Allah that you desire?} That is: do you worship, besides Allah, falsehoods that are not gods and are not fit for worship?! {So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?}: that He would do to you (what you deserve) when you have worshipped others along with Him?! This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. In the authentic hadith: "Abraham (peace be upon him) told only three lies: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it,' and his saying about his wife, 'She is my sister.'" The purpose is that he stayed behind from them so that his plot against their gods would be completed. Hence {they turned their backs and departed}. When he found the opportunity, {he turned to their gods}, that is: he went to them secretly and stealthily, {and said} mockingly to them: {"Will you not eat? What is wrong with you that you do not speak?"}. That is: how is it fitting that they be worshipped when they are inferior even to animals that eat and speak, while these are inanimate objects that neither eat nor speak?! {Then he attacked them, striking with the right hand}: that is, he began striking them with his strength and vigour until he reduced them to fragments, except a large one among them, so that they might return to it.

{94–96} {So they came hastening toward him}: that is, they hurried and rushed, intending to lay hands on him after they had searched. {They said: "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers!"} {It was said: "We heard a youth who mentions them, called Abraham."} He says: {"By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone."} So they rebuked and blamed him. {113} {And We blessed him and Isaac}: that is, We sent down upon them both blessing, which is growth and increase in their knowledge, their deeds and their offspring. Allah spread from their offspring three great nations: the Arab nation from the offspring of Ishmael, the nation of the Children of Israel, and the nation of the Romans from the offspring of Isaac. {And among their offspring are doers of good and those who clearly wrong themselves}: that is, among them are the righteous and the wicked, the just and the unjust, whose wrongdoing is manifest through their disbelief and polytheism. Perhaps this is to remove a misunderstanding: when He said {And We blessed him and Isaac}, that implied blessing in their offspring, and that part of complete blessing is that all their offspring be doers of good; so Allah informed that among them are doers of good and wrongdoers. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verse 83–113:

{83–84} That is: and among the followers of Noah (peace be upon him), and those who followed his path in prophethood, messengership, calling the creation to Allah and answering supplication, was Abraham the Friend (peace be upon him). {When he came to his Lord with a sound heart}: free from shirk, doubts and desires that prevent perceiving the truth and acting upon it. When the heart of a servant is sound, he is safe from every evil and attains every good.

{85–87} Among its soundness is that it is free from deceiving people, envying them, and other bad character traits. For this reason he advised the people for the sake of Allah, beginning with his father and his people, and said: {When he said to his father and his people: "What is it that you worship?"} This is a question in the form of denunciation and a binding of them with proof. {Is it a fabrication, gods other than Allah that you desire?} That is: do you worship, besides Allah, falsehoods that are not gods and are not fit for worship?! {So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?}: that He would do to you (what you deserve) when you have worshipped others along with Him?! This is a warning to them of the requital, the punishment for persisting in their shirk. And what did you suppose of the Lord of the worlds of deficiency, that you made for Him rivals and partners?!

{88–93} So he (peace be upon him) wished to break their idols and to be able to do so. He seized the opportunity when they were heedless, when they went out to one of their festivals, and he went out with them. {Then he glanced at the stars and said: "Indeed, I am sick"}. In the authentic hadith: "Abraham (peace be upon him) told only three lies: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it,' and his saying about his wife, 'She is my sister.'" The purpose is that he stayed behind from them so that his plot against their gods would be completed. Hence {they turned their backs and departed}. When he found the opportunity, {he turned to their gods}, that is: he went to them secretly and stealthily, {and said} mockingly to them: {"Will you not eat? What is wrong with you that you do not speak?"}. That is: how is it fitting that they be worshipped when they are inferior even to animals that eat and speak, while these are inanimate objects that neither eat nor speak?! {Then he attacked them, striking with the right hand}: that is, he began striking them with his strength and vigour until he reduced them to fragments, except a large one among them, so that they might return to it.

{94–96} {So they came hastening toward him}: that is, they hurried and rushed, intending to lay hands on him after they had searched. {They said: "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers!"} {It was said: "We heard a youth who mentions them, called Abraham."} He says: {"By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned away and gone."} So they rebuked and blamed him. He said: {"Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it, so ask them, if they can speak."} {So they returned to themselves and said: "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."} {Then they were turned back upon their heads: "You have certainly known that these do not speak."} He said: {"Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you at all nor harms you...?"} to the end of the verse. And his saying here {"Do you worship what you carve?"}: that is, what you carve with your hands and fashion. So how do you worship them when you are the ones who made them, and leave sincere devotion to Allah, who {created you and what you do}?!

{97–98} {They said: "Build for him a structure"}: that is, a high edifice, and kindle fire in it, {and cast him into the blazing fire}, as requital for what he did in breaking their gods. They intended {a plot against him}: to kill him in the most horrible manner. {So We made them the lowest}: Allah turned their plot back upon their own necks, and made the fire cool and safe for Abraham.

{99} When they did this to him, and he had established the proof against them and excused himself before them, {he said: "Indeed, I am going to my Lord"}: that is, I am emigrating to Him, heading to the blessed land, the land of Sham, {He will guide me}: He will show me what is good for me in my religion and my worldly affairs. And in another verse he said: {"And I will withdraw from you and what you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I will not be unblessed in my calling upon my Lord."}

{100} {"My Lord, grant me"}: a child who would be {among the righteous}. This was when he despaired of his people and saw no good in them; he asked Allah to grant him a righteous son through whom Allah would benefit in his life and after his death.

{101} Allah answered him and said: {So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy}. This is Ishmael (peace be upon him) without doubt; for the good tidings of Isaac is mentioned after it, and because Allah, Exalted, said in the good tidings of Isaac: {So We gave him good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob}. This shows that Isaac is not the one who was sacrificed. Allah described Ishmael (peace be upon him) as forbearing, and this includes patience, good character, breadth of chest, and pardoning those who wrong him.

{102} {Then when he reached with him the age of exertion}: that is, he reached the age to strive alongside him, and attained an age in which he is usually most beloved to his parents; his hardship had gone and his benefit had come. Abraham (peace be upon him) said to him: {"Indeed, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you"}: that is, I have seen in sleep and vision that Allah is commanding me to slaughter you, and the dreams of the prophets are revelation. {So see what you think}: for the command of Allah, Exalted, must be carried out. Ishmael said, patient, seeking reward, pleasing to his Lord and dutiful to his father: {"O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient."} That is: go forward with what Allah has ordered you. He informed his father that he had resolved himself to patience, and he tied that to the will of Allah, Exalted, because nothing happens without the will of Allah.

{103} {And when they had both submitted}: that is, Abraham and his son Ishmael. Abraham was resolved to slaughter his son, the fruit of his heart, in compliance with the command of his Lord and out of fear of His punishment; and the son had resolved himself to patience, finding it easy in obedience to his Lord and in the pleasure of his father. {And he put him down upon his forehead}: that is, Abraham laid Ishmael down on his forehead in order to lay him on his side and slaughter him, having turned him over on his face, lest he look at his face at the time of slaughter.

{104–105} {And We called to him}: in that distressing state and astonishing matter: {"O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision"}: that is, you have done what you were commanded, for you resolved yourself to it, did every means, and nothing remained but to pass the knife over his throat. {Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good}: in Our worship, those who prefer Our pleasure over their own desires.

{106} {Indeed, this}: by which We tested Abraham (peace be upon him), {is truly the manifest trial}: that is, the clear one by which the purity of Abraham and the completeness of his love for his Lord and his intimate friendship were shown. When Allah granted Ishmael to Abraham, he loved him intensely, and he was the Friend of the Merciful. Friendship is the highest kind of love, a station that accepts no sharing, and it requires that all parts of the heart be attached to the Beloved. When a portion of his heart became attached to his son Ishmael, Allah, Exalted, willed to purify his affection and test his friendship, so He commanded him to slaughter what competed his love with the love of his Lord. When he gave precedence to the love of Allah over his own desire, resolved to slaughter him, and what was in the heart of competition was removed, the slaughter remained without benefit; hence He said: {Indeed, this is truly the manifest trial}.

(114–122) He, may He be exalted, mentions His favour upon His two servants and messengers, Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron), the sons of Imran, in bestowing prophethood and messengership upon them and calling (people) to God, and in saving them and their people from their enemy Fir'awn (Pharaoh), and in granting them victory over him, to the point that God drowned him while they were watching. (He also mentions) God's sending down to them both the Clear Book, which is the Tawrah (Torah), containing the rulings, the admonitions, and the detailed explanation of everything; and that God guided them both to the Straight Path, by legislating for them a religion with straight rulings and laws that lead to God, and by bestowing upon them the grace of following it.

﴿And We left for them both among later generations: "Peace be upon Musa and Harun."﴾ That is: He preserved for them both a good remembrance and a greeting among later generations, and all the more so among earlier ones. ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, they were among Our believing servants.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verses 133–138:

{133–138} This is a praise from Allah, exalted is He, of His servant and messenger Lut (Lot), by (conferring upon him) prophethood and messengership, and of his calling his people to Allah and forbidding them from shirk (associating partners with Allah) and from committing the abomination. When they did not desist, Allah rescued him and his family, all of them, so they set out by night and were saved. ﴿Except an old woman, among those who remained behind﴾; i.e., among those who remained behind and were punished. She was the wife of Lut, and she was not upon his religion. ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾: by overturning their dwellings, so We made its uppermost part its lowermost, and rained down upon them stones of hard clay, layered and piled up, until they were extinguished and quenched. ﴿And indeed you pass by them﴾; i.e., by the dwellings of the people of Lut, ﴿in the morning, and at night﴾; i.e., at these times your coming and going past them is frequent, ﴿so will you not reason?﴾ regarding the signs and lessons, and refrain from that which brings about destruction?!

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verses 139–148:**

{139} This is a praise from Him, exalted is He, upon His servant and messenger Yunus ibn Matta (Jonah son of Matthew), just as He praised His other messenger brothers with prophethood, messengership, and calling to God.

{140} God, exalted is He, mentioned about him that He punished him with a worldly punishment, from which He saved him because of his faith and righteous deeds. He said: ﴿When he fled﴾; that is, from his Lord, angry with Him, thinking that He would not have power over him, and [the fish] would imprison him in the belly of the whale. God did not mention what he was angry about, nor the sin he committed, because there is no benefit for us in mentioning it. Our benefit lies only in what we have mentioned about him: that he sinned, that God punished him despite being one of the noble messengers, that He then saved him, removed blame from him, and destined for him what would be the cause of his righteousness. So when he fled, he took refuge in ﴿the laden ship﴾: laden with riders and goods.

{141} When he boarded with others while the ship was full, the vessel became heavy, and they needed to throw off some of the riders. It seemed that they found no one deserving of preference in that, so they drew lots, agreeing that whoever was chosen by the lot and defeated would be thrown into the sea, as a fair measure among the people of the ship. When God wills a matter, He prepares its causes. When they drew lots, the lot fell upon Yunus. ﴿So he was among the losers﴾; that is, the defeated, and he was thrown into the sea.

{142} ﴿Then the whale swallowed him while he was﴾ at the time of swallowing ﴿blameworthy﴾; that is, doing what deserves blame, which is his being angry with his Lord.

{143–144} ﴿Had he not been among those who glorify God﴾; that is, in his earlier time through his abundant worship of his Lord, His glorification and praise, and in the belly of the whale when he said: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾; ﴿he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾; that is, it would have become his grave. But because of his glorification and worship of God, God saved him, and thus God saves the believers when they fall into hardships.

{145} ﴿So We cast him onto the barren land﴾: the whale cast him out of its belly onto the barren land, which is the empty land, bare of anyone, and perhaps even bare of trees and shade. ﴿While he was ailing﴾; that is, he had become sick and weak because of his confinement in the belly of the whale, until he became like a fledgling plucked from its egg.

{146} ﴿And We caused to grow over him a gourd plant﴾: providing shade with its dense shade, because its shade is cool, and no fly lands on it. This is from God's gentleness and kindness toward him.

{147–148} Then He treated him with another gentleness and bestowed upon him a great favor: He sent him ﴿to a hundred thousand﴾ people ﴿or more﴾. The meaning is that if they were not more, they were not less. He called them to God, exalted is He, and ﴿they believed﴾, so they became within His scales, because he was their caller. ﴿So We gave them enjoyment for a time﴾: God turned away the punishment from them after its causes had been set in motion. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time.﴾

{149} Allah says to His Prophet (ﷺ), {So ask them (fa-istaftihim)}; that is: ask the polytheists, who worshipped the angels and claimed that they are the daughters of Allah, "by Allah" (or: concerning Allah) — they combined associating partners with Allah with attributing to Him what does not befit His majesty. {Has your Lord got daughters while they have sons?} That is: this is an unjust division and a wrongful statement, in that they attributed offspring to Allah, the Exalted, and in that they made for Him the worse and more contemptible of the two kinds, namely daughters, which they themselves would not be pleased to have. As He said in another verse: {And they attribute to Allah daughters—glory be to Him—while for themselves they have what they desire} [An-Nahl 16:57]. And also in that they made the angels daughters of Allah and judged that.

{150} Allah, the Exalted, says in explaining their lie: {Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?} That is, of their creation: the matter is not so, for they did not witness their creation. This shows that they said this statement without knowledge, rather it is a fabrication against Allah.

How do you judge?} — this unjust judgment. {Will you not then remember?} — and distinguish this false and unjust statement? For if you had remembered, you would not have said this statement. {Or do you have a clear authority?} — that is, a manifest proof for your claim from a Book or a messenger. But all of this is not the case, and therefore He said: {Then bring your Book, if you are truthful.} For whoever says a statement for which he has no legitimate proof is either a deliberate liar or one who speaks about Allah without knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 37, verses 167–182:

{167–170} Almighty Allah informs that these polytheists would express wishing and say: "If we had been given a Reminder and scriptures like those given to the earlier peoples, we would have been sincere in worship to Allah; indeed, we would have been truly sincere." But they are liars in this, for the best of books came to them and they disbelieved in it. It is thus known that they are rebellious against the truth. {So they will come to know} the punishment when it befalls them.

{171–179} Nor should they think that they will be victorious in this world. Rather, the word of Allah has already preceded, the word which cannot be turned back or opposed, for His servants, the messengers, and His soldiers, the successful: that they are the victorious over others, and they will be helped by their Lord with a mighty help, by which they will be enabled to establish their religion. This is a great good tiding for whoever is characterized as being among the soldiers of Allah, by having upright conditions and by fighting those against whom he has been commanded to fight, that he is victorious and helped. Then He commanded His Messenger to turn away from those who were obstinate and did not accept the truth, and that there remains only to await the punishment that will descend upon them. Therefore He said: {And see them, for they will see}: whoever will be struck by the retribution; for it will surely descend upon them. {When it descends upon their courtyard}, that is, descends upon them and near them, {evil is the morning of those who were warned}, because it is a morning of evil, punishment and annihilation. Then He repeated the command to turn away from them and the threat of the punishment's occurrence.

{180–182} When this surah mentioned many of their abominable statements by which they described Him, He declared Himself exempt from them, saying: {Glory be to your Lord}, that is, He is exalted and high above; {the Lord of might}, that is, the One who is mighty and overcomes everything, and who is exalted above every evil with which they describe Him. {And peace be upon the messengers}: because of their freedom from sins and afflictions, and the soundness of what they were described with by the Originator of the earth and the heavens. {And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds}: the alif and lam are for totality; so all kinds of praise belong to Allah, from the perfect and mighty attributes and the actions by which He nurtured the worlds, bestowed upon them blessings, averted from them calamities, and managed them in their movements and stillness and in all their conditions. He, Exalted is He, is free from every deficiency, praised for every perfection, beloved and magnified. His messengers are safe and greeted with peace, and whoever follows them in that has safety in this world and the Hereafter, while His enemies have destruction and ruin in this world and the Hereafter.

The tafsir of Surat al-Saffat was completed on the 6th of Shawwal, 1343 AH, by its compiler and scribe, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir al-Sa'di.
May Allah send blessings and peace upon Muhammad (ﷺ), and peace abundantly. And praise be to Allah, through whose grace good deeds are completed.

Then He commanded His Messenger to turn away from those who were obstinate and did not accept the truth, and that there remains only to await the punishment that will descend upon them. Therefore He said: {And see them, for they will see}: whoever will be struck by the retribution; for it will surely descend upon them. {When it descends upon their courtyard}, that is, descends upon them and near them, {evil is the morning of those who were warned}, because it is a morning of evil, punishment and annihilation. Then He repeated the command to turn away from them and the threat of the punishment's occurrence.

{180–182} When this surah mentioned many of their abominable statements by which they described Him, He declared Himself exempt from them, saying: {Glory be to your Lord}, that is, He is exalted and high above; {the Lord of might}, that is, the One who is mighty and overcomes everything, and who is exalted above every evil with which they describe Him. {And peace be upon the messengers}: because of their freedom from sins and afflictions, and the soundness of what they were described with by the Originator of the earth and the heavens. {And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds}: the alif and lam are for totality; so all kinds of praise belong to Allah, from the perfect and mighty attributes and the actions by which He nurtured the worlds, bestowed upon them blessings, averted from them calamities, and managed them in their movements and stillness and in all their conditions. He, Exalted is He, is free from every deficiency, praised for every perfection, beloved and magnified. His messengers are safe and greeted with peace, and whoever follows them in that has safety in this world and the Hereafter, while His enemies have destruction and ruin in this world and the Hereafter.

The tafsir of Surat al-Saffat was completed on the 6th of Shawwal, 1343 AH, by its compiler and scribe, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir al-Sa'di.
May Allah send blessings and peace upon Muhammad (ﷺ), and peace abundantly. And praise be to Allah, through whose grace good deeds are completed.
